A1.justification: Both complete 56-page PDFs describe the same AP-MDM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–P are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AP-MDM experiments on Sudoku, graph editing and parity in Section 5, Figures 3–4 and Appendices N–P. The Sudoku comparator results are explicitly attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Sudoku, graph-editing and parity experiments and their reported outcomes, including AP-MDM's 99.28% Sudoku accuracy.

M1.justification: The AP-MDM architecture, remask/insert/delete operations, transition function, training objectives and inference algorithm are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Sudoku, graph editing through minimum-cut computation, and parity length generalization. Coding and DNA recombination remain theoretical or illustrative examples; no experimental domain or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Sudoku retains both ARM variants and all three AO-MDM variants; graph and parity retain their ARM comparisons. The Sudoku source changes from Kim et al. (2025b) to (2025c) through citation relabeling. Newly cited editing models are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The training configurations, sample counts, metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. Appendix D and Appendices N–P retain the same model configurations, training budgets and task-specific data-generation procedures.

E4.justification: The Sudoku loss-convergence analysis, graph-size comparison, parity length-generalization analysis and appendix operation examples are retained. No ablation, robustness test or substantive supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point accuracies, training/validation curves and descriptive sequence-length statistics. Neither introduces repeated-run information, uncertainty intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: Figures 3–4 retain identical result panels: Sudoku accuracy remains 99.28%, graph accuracies are unchanged, and the parity curves coincide. Table 1 and the experimental appendices are also unchanged. Figure 2(d)'s corrected nucleotide labels concern an illustrative schematic, not experimental findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements and proofs are unchanged, including the PRAM simulations, Dyck-language construction and editing-simulation hardness argument. Earlier appendix differences are pagination and movement around algorithms.

C1.justification: The introduction refines the broad statement that ARM cannot generate arbitrary-length matched parentheses into a limitation on covering the entire two-sided Dyck-k support with constant-depth Transformers. This better matches the existing theorem; the principal computational and empirical contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The expanded introductory explanations concerning global foresight and the difficulty of simulating edits already appear in Sections 5.2 and 5.4 of v1. The interpretations of sample efficiency, generalization and applicability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A new LLM-use statement discloses assistance with code writing and debugging, adding limited implementation provenance without identifying specific tools or settings. The technical appendices, hyperparameters, data-generation instructions and code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds earlier insertion, editing and permutation approaches, including Insertion Transformer, Levenshtein Transformer, XLNet, LaserTagger and Mask-Predict, plus Kim et al.'s self-correction work. It clarifies the distinction between these predecessors and the paper's unified computational analysis. Two bibliography entries are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten to summarize specific theoretical findings, one introductory contribution paragraph is expanded and renamed, related work gains a paragraph, and an LLM-use disclosure is added. These are localized revisions; the overall organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2(d) changes two C labels to A, correcting the illustrated DNA recombination products. Added prose causes local pagination and placement changes, but no figure or table is added or removed, and the result displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more informative abstract, a more precise introductory Dyck-language claim, and better acknowledgment of earlier editing-based generation methods in Appendix A. The DNA schematic correction also improves accuracy. These are useful improvements in clarity and positioning, while the methods, proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
